source.title: On Learning Contrastive Representations for Learning with Noisy Labels
source.authors: Linya Yi; Sheng Liu; Qi She; A. McLeod; Bo-Yu Wang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendix; some figure and table layout is flattened.
record.tranche_reason: Compares label-noise memorization under cross-entropy and contrastive representations, measuring predictions on wrongly labeled examples after fine-tuning a linear classifier on frozen representations. This is a different setup from training an end-to-end network on completely random labels.
record.gate_note: The study measures memorization only for 80% symmetric and 40% asymmetric label noise in Figure 3. Its CIFAR noise-level tables report test accuracy, not training-set fit or memorization. The claim that conventional memorization increases during training is attributed to prior work, not measured here.
record.test_reason: The study uses label memorization to motivate a mitigation method. Its direct memorization experiment trains an underparameterized linear classifier on frozen representations previously learned with clean labels, rather than training a deep network on corrupted labels. The remaining experiments report test accuracy without establishing training-set memorization. Neither establishes the behavior specified by a claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. More precisely, the authors theoretically argue that ideal contrastive representations retain true-label information while discarding corrupted-label information, and propose CTRR to learn robust representations from noisy data. Their experiments demonstrate improved test accuracy and reduced memorization in the separate frozen-representation experiment.
record.recipe_differences: Adds a contrastive regularization term and compares linear-classifier fine-tuning on frozen representations; does not reproduce the original random-label training setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured memorization settings differ by noise type and level: 80% symmetric and 40% asymmetric label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: CTR representations yield less corrupted-label agreement than CE representations when a newly initialized linear classifier is trained on frozen representations learned with clean labels. The authors explicitly report decreasing memorization during this training and attribute it to underparameterization, with a parameter-to-sample ratio around 0.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clean-label contrastive representations can reduce noisy-label memorization by an underparameterized linear classifier trained on frozen features.

record.problems: The claim-relevant memorization outcomes are shown only in Figure 3, with no numerical values or uncertainty available in the supplied text. The measured classifier is a linear layer on frozen representations, and only two label-noise settings are shown.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were left out. Test-accuracy tables are not rows because they do not measure training-set fit or memorization.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, near-zero deep-network training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time and convergence speed as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect deep-network training fit across a corruption sweep while test error approaches chance. Tables 1–2 report declining CE test accuracy, but do not establish simultaneous memorization or include completely random labeling.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting, and generalization after removing them.
The temporal ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noise in deep networks. Early learning is invoked from prior work rather than independently measured.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V4 limits_scope verdict: deliberately freezing representations and training an underparameterized classifier does not qualify the claim about deep networks fitting noisy training sets. Figure 3's qualitative comparison is stated in the text, but its absolute memorization levels cannot be recovered from the supplied extraction.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture or hyperparameters.
Training-time cost and how convergence changes with the fraction of corrupted labels.

The study does not test a sweep from no corruption to complete random labeling, perfect training fit across that sweep, or whether the measured effect reflects end-to-end network training; it fine-tunes a linear classifier on frozen representations.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent random-label fitting, or whether removing them harms generalization on true labels.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels during training.

rows.subject: Resnet34
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tune the linear classifier on noisy labels with frozen representations learned using CE.
rows.measure: Fraction of wrongly labeled examples whose predictions equal their labels (memorization).
rows.note: Figure text defines memorization as matching corrupted labels. The authors state that CTR representations show reduced memorization, but the figure values are not available as numbers in the supplied text.
rows.check: Measures a linear classifier on frozen, clean-label-trained CE representations, not end-to-end deep-network fitting under V4. Absolute memorization values are unreadable in the supplied text, so 'partial' is unsupported. ResNet34 is specified for Figure 2, but not established for Figure 3.

rows.subject: Resnet34
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tune the linear classifier on noisy labels with frozen representations learned using CTR.
rows.measure: Fraction of wrongly labeled examples whose predictions equal their labels (memorization).
rows.note: The authors describe reduced memorization with the CTR representation; exact values are figure-only.
rows.check: Measures a linear classifier on frozen, clean-label-trained CTR representations. Reduced memorization relative to CE does not establish incomplete deep-network training fit under V4. Absolute values are unavailable, and the Figure 3 backbone is not established as ResNet34.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10 with 80% symmetric or 40% asymmetric label noise, using a linear classifier on frozen representations
reader_labels.reason: The authors report reduced memorization with CTR representations, so the measured setup does not show persistent full memorization across these conditions (R1–R4). The study does not test the full noise-fraction sweep or perfect training fit.
